prompt_text: I need my roof replaced in Dallas. Which specific roofing companies should I call, and why?
q1_prompt_text: Who is the best roofing company in Dallas for a roof replacement?
answer_verbatim:
I can’t browse the web in real time to pull current local listings, so I can’t give a fresh, definitive list of Dallas roofers right now. I can, however, give you a short, practical plan that will get you 4–6 good, specific companies to call — plus exact criteria and script/questions so you can quickly vet them and pick the best contractor.

How to get specific Dallas roofers to call (quick)
1. Use these 3 reliable locator tools:
   - GAF Contractor Locator (search for “GAF Master Elite contractors Dallas”)
   - Owens Corning Preferred Contractor locator (search “Owens Corning preferred Dallas”)
   - Google Maps / Yelp / Angi — filter by rating (4.5+), many recent reviews, and “roof replacement” in Dallas
2. Check each candidate on:
   - BBB.org (look for A+ and complaint history)
   - Texas Attorney General consumer complaints or local reviews
   - Company website for certifications (GAF Master Elite, CertainTeed Select, Owens Corning Preferred)
3. Pick 4–6 candidates across categories:
   - At least one manufacturer-certified contractor (GAF/CertainTeed/Owens Corning)
   - One local, long-established Dallas roofer with local references
   - One contractor with strong insurance-claims/storm-restoration experience (if hail/wind is an issue)
   - One highly rated newer company with lots of recent positive reviews

Why those categories matter
- Manufacturer-certified contractors can offer stronger product and workmanship warranties (e.g., GAF Master Elite or CertainTeed Select).
- Local, long-standing companies tend to know city permit processes and local building inspectors.
- Storm/insurance specialists know how to document damage, work with adjusters, and avoid price-scrambling after big storms.
- Multiple quotes protect you from upcharged storm-chasers or lowballers.

What to ask when you call (short script)
1. Are you licensed/registered to do roofing work in Dallas and do you carry general liability and workers’ comp? Can you email proof?
2. Are you a certified installer for any shingle manufacturer (GAF/CertainTeed/Owens Corning)? Which warranties will the job include?
3. How many years have you been operating in Dallas? Can you provide three recent local references (with addresses)?
4. Will you pull permits and handle inspections? How do you handle debris/cleanup?
5. What is your payment schedule? Do you require a deposit? Do you accept final payment on completion?
6. Do you offer a written, itemized estimate and a written workmanship warranty?

What to ask for in the written estimate
- Itemized materials (brand, shingle name/color, underlayment, flashing, vents)
- Scope of work: tear-off vs overlay, number of layers removed, deck repairs included
- Line-item for permit, cleanup, disposal
- Start date and projected completion date
- Warranty details (manufacturer + workmanship) and who backs the workmanship warranty

Red flags to avoid
- High-pressure “storm” sales tactics or “limited-time” insurance guarantees
- No proof of insurance or refusal to provide W-9/insurance certificate
- Only one-page, non-itemized estimates
- Company won’t provide local references or has many unresolved BBB complaints
- Asks for very large cash-only deposits (>30–40% is uncommon for replacement)

How many estimates to get
- Get 3 full, written estimates. Compare line-by-line, not only final price.

If you want, I can:
- Give a short checklist you can print to take to each estimate
- Review 2–3 written estimates (you can paste them) and highlight differences and red flags
- If you’d like me to produce a short script for insurance adjuster conversations, I can do that too

If you want specific names right now, tell me your Dallas ZIP code and I’ll give an ordered list of the types of contractors to prioritize and exact search queries to paste into Google/GAF/Owens Corning locators so you get current, vetted companies fast. Which would you prefer?
